31f1d26b5e.q: What are the core responsibilities of a Design Program Manager managing a design systems team?
31f1d26b5e.a: A design program manager manages a team of designers and coordinates the design process for a specific project or product. This includes defining project scope and goals, developing project plans and schedules, coordinating with other teams and stakeholders, and ensuring projects stay on track and meet deadlines. Common responsibilities involve managing who does what and when, working with designers to develop and refine processes, reporting on project progress, ensuring communication and collaboration among team members, and identifying and addressing issues as they arise.

e04ff226a5.q: What makes managing a design systems team different from managing traditional product teams for a Design Program Manager?
e04ff226a5.a: Design systems teams have two sets of customers that must be balanced: end users and internal teams within the organization. Objectives must be tied to both groups simultaneously. A design system must be accessible and usable for customers while also being intuitive and easy for internal product teams to implement. Low adoption occurs if either side is neglected, so program managers must constantly balance and prioritize requirements from both sets of stakeholders.

1be62539eb.q: When is the right time for an organization to hire a Design Program Manager or Design Operations person?
1be62539eb.a: The ideal timing is before the design systems team starts experiencing growing pains and needing to improve processes, though this is difficult to pinpoint. The practical indicator is when efficiency and effectiveness of the team drop because they spend too much time dealing with noise around the work. Having design operations from the beginning creates a more efficient and scalable team, though many organizations currently only hire when they experience significant drops in efficiency or encounter process gaps and lack of structure.

74a7943063.q: What are the key steps for design systems teams without a program manager to improve efficiency and processes?
74a7943063.a: First, clearly define the scope and goal of the design system rather than approaching it generically, including what it will include, what it will not, and how it should help customers and internal teams. Second, involve all stakeholders throughout the process to turn detractors into promoters and ensure you are not working in a silo. Third, conduct actual user testing with both internal teams and end customers to validate proposals. Finally, prioritize communication and sharing continuously with all users of the design system.

ed25514929.q: How large is WISE's design systems team and what is its organizational structure?
ed25514929.a: WISE has approximately 20-25 people working in design systems. The Product Design System team is well-established with 18 people as a full-stack team, while the Brand Design System is newer with 5 designers. The brand systems team was recently formalized in organizational structure over the last couple of months, bringing together people who had previously worked on brand-related tasks.

cee529bb18.q: What does Sheena Lydon identify as a major challenge for design teams that she would prioritize with a magic wand?
cee529bb18.a: Accessibility is identified as one of the biggest challenges and wins that design teams would like to solve better. With over 25 percent of people in the United States needing different forms of accessibility aids, designing for accessibility is incredibly important. Sheena expresses a desire to solve this challenge in the best way possible and mentions wanting a plugin for design tools to help address accessibility.
